Capture date: 2026-11-16 (UTC). Salesforce CLI: 2.157.8.
Orgs: five fresh Developer scratch orgs (1-day lifetime) from campaign Dev Hubs, each deployed with the synthetic project in this directory (objects, matching rules, duplicate rules, DupProbe) and a System Administrator profile grant of the fixture fields. Each org was deleted and verified gone after its run (the delete command answered, the local target stopped resolving). Two earlier deployments that failed validation were also deleted and wrote no rows.
APIs: 62.0 (org A: keys ORD*..OPT_alrt plus REP; org C: SGATE*, FDIFF2; org E: SGATE2, FCASE) and 67.0 (org B: all first-round keys plus REP; org D: SGATE2, FCASE). Apex was deployed and the anonymous and @IsTest runs were requested at the matching API; 62.0 and 67.0 rows agree for every key.
Routes: anonymous Apex (sf apex run --api-version) and an @IsTest class (sf apex run test), the same DupProbe.emit(key) expression. For every key the anonymous and @IsTest payloads are identical. REP rows are committed anonymous runs: REPW writes, REPR and REPR2 read DuplicateRecordSet/Item in later requests (the second read is a repeat).
Transport: a failed assertion carries DUPOBS|key|JSON. Payloads label records by the Name Apex assigned and contain no ids except object ids and record ids that appear in platform messages; those were replaced by <id> when the rows were committed. Entity tokens that the platform reported as object ids for empty results are likewise <id>.
Round structure: round one ran ORD*, ORD2*, GATE*, X99, CAPQ, XMAP, NOREG, MIXT, FDIFF, OPT_blk, OPT_alrt and REP at both APIs; SGATE* and FDIFF2 ran at 67.0 first and at 62.0 afterwards; SGATE2 and FCASE are the follow-up probes for the update gate and the Exact comparison.
Rule filters use one Mode text field per object because the deployment resolves a duplicate-rule filter field by name across the whole deploy.

Second capture (2026-11-16 UTC, Salesforce CLI 2.156.8): two fresh Developer scratch orgs (1-day lifetime) from a campaign Dev Hub, one deployed at 62.0 and one at 67.0 with the same synthetic project, DupProbe extended by the RPT_* and ENT keys and the RPTM_*, RPTN_*, RPTO_* phase keys. Each org was deleted and verified gone (the delete answered, the local target stopped resolving). 62.0 and 67.0 rows agree for every new key, and the anonymous and @IsTest payloads of every single-transaction key are identical.
RPT_same, RPT_other, RPT_ctrl, RPT_alrt, RPT_allow and ENT are single-transaction probes (anonymous and @IsTest). RPTM_1..5, RPTN_1..4 and RPTO_1..5 are one anonymous request each against the same org, so every step is its own transaction; their rows use the committed_anonymous route.
ENT: the platform reports, for an empty custom-object result, the object's 15-character CustomObject id (01I) as the match-level entity type, and the object name at the DuplicateResult level. Before committing, each 01I token was compared with the object's Id from a Tooling API CustomObject query of the same org (all equal), then masked as <id> like every other id in the rows.
